learning: Race 3 will decide between geometry and gain. If s-bend and slalom line_loss falls below 1 with max_error under 0.06, keep the geometry and tune base_speed for completion time. If line loss stays at 1 or more, the spread is not the limit: hold the geometry and raise kp toward 3.2 before any further geometry change. If oval steering_oscillation is above 0.4, reduce kd or kp by about 0.3 first.
notes: Integrator package for the Builder's ±0.04 m, 16 mm geometry, with kp raised to 2.8 to offset the lower signal slope, kd 0.5 for oval oscillation, and base_speed 1.05 for recovery time. Based on race 2 line-loss evidence (1.1 per run on s-bend and slalom) and the reach model.
rationale: Race 2 (16 mm footprints, ±0.03 m spread, y=0.05, kp 2.4, kd 0.45, base 1.1) scored 356.98. Oval improved to 15/20 finishes with max_error 0.048, but s-bend and slalom still end 40/40 off_track with line_loss about 1.1 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Under the rule we agreed, line loss at or above 1 with max_error at the limit means reach is still the bottleneck, so I accept the Builder's ±0.04 m spread with 16 mm footprints, y=0.05 and five sensors. Reach model: a sensor at lateral x sees tape while |x − e| < about 0.02 m, so outer sensors at ±0.04 m reach e ≈ 0.06 m, the drift at which race 2 lost the line. Gain: with the same weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], the signal slope per metre of offset falls from about 67/m (±0.03 spread) to 50/m (±0.04 spread). kp 2.4 × 67 ≈ 160 per metre, so I raise kp to 2.8 (2.8 × 50 = 140/m). That is slightly less steering per metre than race 2, because the wider footprint pair already supplies earlier signal. kd stays at 0.5 to damp the oval oscillation (0.31 in race 2). base_speed drops to 1.05 to give more recovery time on the tight tracks, since s-bend and slalom have never finished. ki stays at 0 and line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result, not yet measured: line_loss on s-bend and slalom below 1, max_error below 0.06, and oval finish rate at or above 0.7. If line loss stays at 1 or more, the next race should test gain or speed, not geometry.
